transcriptText:
The price says fold. Can chips you win later change that? Pick one. Always call a draw... or only if you can win enough later? Hold that thought.

Eight-seven of spades, on a two-spade board. They bet 45 into 100, with 300 behind. Call, and the pot's 190. Your price... 23.7%. Nine spades left, of 46 cards... 19.6%. The price alone says fold.

But when a spade lands, you can win more of their stack. Your call, divided by your chance, minus the pot. 230 − 190... 40. Win 40 more when you hit, and your price drops to 19.6%. Exactly your chance. Over 46 rivers, you break even.

Now give them only 25 behind. You can't win chips they don't have. Best case, 20.9%. Still too high. Fold.

Your turn. Jack-ten, four outs. Pot 60, bet 20, 90 behind. You'd need 130 more... only 90's there. Fold. So... always call a draw? No. Count what you can still win, and stop at their stack. Up next: stack-to-pot ratio.
